cards.explanation: The first book runs right up to the day He was taken up to heaven. The writer says it covers all that Jesus began to do and to teach, "…until the day He was taken up to heaven…" (Acts 1:2). So the book runs right up to that exact day, friends. Quite the stretch for one book.

The answer is apostles. Jesus gave instructions through the Holy Spirit to "…the apostles He had chosen." (Acts 1:2). Chosen is the key word there, friends. He picked them Himself, and I think that's worth sitting with for a second.

The answer is True. After His suffering, Jesus presented Himself to the apostles "…with many convincing proofs that He was alive." (Acts 1:3). Many proofs, friends, not just one. I think if I'd seen that, I'd have needed to sit down and fan myself with a cookie sheet.

The answer is the gift the Father promised. Jesus says, "Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift the Father promised, which you have heard Me discuss." (Acts 1:4). They'd already heard Him talk about it, friends. Now the job was to stay put and wait.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "…in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit." (Acts 1:5). Just a few days, friends, not many years. That's why He tells them to stay in Jerusalem and wait.

The answer is that they ask Him to restore the kingdom to Israel. They ask, "Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?" (Acts 1:6). The passage says earlier that Jesus spoke about the kingdom of God (Acts 1:3). I respect a crew that just asks, bakers.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority." (Acts 1:7). The Father fixed them, friends, and they're not the apostles' to know. I think that's a relief, honestly.
The answer is witnesses. Jesus says, "…you will be My witnesses…" (Acts 1:8). A witness tells what they've seen and heard, friends. That's a big job, and they were handed it straight from Jesus.

The answer is to the ends of the earth. Jesus says they'll be His witnesses "…in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth." (Acts 1:8). It starts with Jerusalem and goes all the way out, bakers. That's a long list, and the last item is HUGE.

The answer is a cloud. The verse says, "…they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight." (Acts 1:9). They watched the whole thing until the cloud covered Him. Nothing fancy added, friends.

The answer is True. The verse says they "…were looking intently into the sky as He was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them." (Acts 1:10). Suddenly is the word, friends. One second it's just them and the sky, and the next there are two more.

The answer is that He will come back the same way He went. The two men say, "This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven." (Acts 1:11). That's why my ovens stay ready, friends. As for when, Jesus says no one knows the day or the hour except the Father (Matthew 24:36).
